title: Hello and goodbye
canDo: greet someone, say goodbye and be polite

dialogue.setting: Priya has just moved into an apartment building in Ottawa. She stops at the front desk to ask the building manager, Mr. Gagnon, for a form.

lines.speaker: M. Gagnon
lines.en: Very well, thank you. And you?

lines.speaker: Priya
lines.fr: Bien, merci. Un formulaire, s'il vous plaît.
lines.en: Fine, thank you. A form, please.

lines.speaker: M. Gagnon
lines.en: You're welcome! Have a good day!

vocabulary.note: Used all day, until early evening.
Used from about 6 p.m. to greet someone. To say goodbye in the evening, use Bonne soirée !
Informal: friends, family and children only.
Used for any adult woman, married or not.
Informal. The answer can also be Ça va: "It's going fine."
Formal. With friends: s'il te plaît.

vocabulary.canadianNote: In Quebec, bienvenue is a common reply to merci. In France it only means "welcome".

vocabulary.en: here you go, there it is

grammar.title: Formal and informal greetings
explanation: French has a formal way and an informal way to talk to someone. Use the formal way with people you don't know, at work, and in shops and offices. Use the informal way with friends, family and children.
When in doubt, be formal. In this unit you speak formally and only need to recognise the informal greetings. You'll learn to use them in unit 3.

examples.en: Goodbye, sir. Have a good day! (formal)

explanation: Most consonants at the end of a French word are not pronounced: the s in vous, the t in salut, the z in allez, the p in beaucoup.
A final e is usually silent too, as in madame.
The letters c, r, f and l are often pronounced at the end of a word. Think of the English word "careful". You hear the r in bonjour.

examples.en: please (silent s in vous, silent t in plaît)

exercises.prompt: You meet your new manager. How do you ask how they are?
Someone says "Merci !" to you. What can you answer?

drills.en: Very well, thank you. And you?

canDoCheck.prompt: You walk into a Service Canada office at 10 a.m. What do you say first?
The clerk hands you a form. What do you say?
